previous_statement: Set S=sigma(U), a unitary by node 1.5. The correction estimates give ||mu(S,U)-S bold-dot U||<=84*epsilon_r and ||S-U^dagger||<=84*epsilon_r. Therefore ||S bold-dot U-U^dagger bold-dot U||<(1+1/64)*84*2*epsilon_r<171*epsilon_r. Since U^dagger bold-dot U=J, the left-inverse defect is below 255*epsilon_r, hence at most 260*epsilon_r.
new_statement: Take P,q from lem-stage1-polar-retraction and choose C_pol=P, kappa_pol=min(q,1/64), C_grp=600. The self-contained descendants below derive directly from these hypotheses, the two allowed polar externals, and the registered definitions that S=sigma(U)=u_delta(U^dagger) is unitary, ||S-U^dagger||<=84*epsilon_r, and ||mu(S,U)-S bold-dot U||<=84*epsilon_r. They also derive epsilon_r<=1/64 and ||U||<=2. Hence ||S bold-dot U-U^dagger bold-dot U||<=171*epsilon_r; because U^dagger bold-dot U=J, ||mu(sigma(U),U)-J||<=255*epsilon_r<=260*epsilon_r.
